newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-NIGERIAN OFFICIALS REFUSED SWEDISH VISAS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-NIGERIAN OFFICIALS REFUSED SWEDISH VISAS.

text.p: Two Nigerian swimming officials have been refused entry to Sweden for the world short course championships in Gothenburg later this month, sports officials said on Wednesday.

The Nigerians, both members of swimming's international governing body FINA, were refused visas in line with a European Union sanction imposed on Nigeria in 1995 to protest about human rights abuses in the west African country.
Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter named the officials as Doctor Olu Asekun and Chief Thomas.
Sweden's Swimming Association on Wednesday appealed to FINA to try to find a way for the two officials to attend the championships, which start on April 14.
"It is a bit awkward and rather embarrassing that this has happened," the association's manager Olle Axling said.
"We are trying to get FINA and the Foreign Affairs Department to work this out."
A spokesman for Sweden's Foreign Affairs Ministry, Staffan Bjorck, said he was looking into the issue.
He said it seemed the two officials were refused visas by the Swedish embassy in Lagos.
"According to the EU decision this would be right. The reasons for the EU decision were very clear," Bjorck said.
The EU has restricted the right of Nigerian officials and military personnel to travel to or stay in EU states.
The restrictions were first adopted in December 1995, after the execution of writer Ken Saro-Wiwa by the Nigerian regime, and were extended for another six months last December.
